key_insight: A deep neural operator can learn the solution operator for free boundary problems, predicting both field values and moving boundaries with high accuracy and much faster inference than traditional solvers.
problem_solved: Free boundary problems (PDEs with unknown, moving boundaries) are computationally expensive and hard to solve repeatedly for different conditions; this work provides a data-driven operator that generalizes across conditions for rapid, accurate predictions.
method: Train a deep neural operator to map input problem parameters and initial/boundary data to the full spatio-temporal solution and the evolving free boundary.
Generate paired simulation data (varying conditions) and optimize the operator to reproduce both field dynamics and boundary motion, enabling generalization to new instances.
Deploy the trained operator for near real-time inference, enabling fast simulations for downstream tasks (e.g., clinical scenario exploration).
impact: This approach extends operator learning to moving-boundary PDEs, offering AI/ML practitioners a tool for fast, generalizable physics simulations—useful for model-based decision support, rapid parameter sweeps, and clinical applications like tumour-growth prediction.
visual_elements: Schematic: operator network mapping inputs (parameters, initial condition) → solution field + evolving free boundary
Comparison bar/line chart: accuracy vs runtime for neural operator vs classical numerical solvers
Pipeline flow: data generation → operator training → real-time inference (with an example tumour-growth timeline)
Heatmap/time-lapse frames: predicted field and boundary evolution across time for several test cases
paper_title: Deep neural operator for free boundary problems
paper_authors: Zongjia Long, Qi Zhou, Aiqing Zhu, Dong Dai, Yiqun Liu
